summary: Chickpea fritters: cooked chickpeas pulsed in a food processor with green onion, garlic, rosemary, lemon, an egg, flour, breadcrumbs and toasted sesame seeds, formed into 3-inch patties and shallow-fried about 3 minutes per side; makes 16 in 30 minutes as an appetizer, side or protein-packed main.
glance: 3 cups cooked (two 15-ounce cans, drained and rinsed)
a few tablespoons of oil, medium-high, about 3 minutes per side until golden brown
faq: How are these like falafel?
Somewhat like a pan-fried falafel, but without a deep-fried crust, so the internal flavoring (green onion, garlic, rosemary, lemon, sesame) is amped up.
How do I know the mixture is right?

Buzz until fairly uniform but stop before completely pureed: you want some texture left. You should be able to form it into a ball that holds its shape, neither crumbly nor a batter; add liquid or breadcrumbs as necessary.
How do I shape and fry them?

Take a golf-ball-sized piece, press it into a flattened 3-inch patty and fry in a few tablespoons of oil in a large (preferably cast-iron) skillet over medium-high heat until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side. Drain on paper towels and finish with flaky sea salt.
How should I serve them?
As an appetizer, a side dish, or the protein-packed star of the show. The author suggests the Tomato Jam with Rosemary and Saffron for a big flavor combination.
Can I use canned chickpeas?
Yes: two 15-ounce cans, drained and rinsed, equal 3 cups.

summary: Butternut squash soup with maple pumpkin seeds: squash browned with onion, celery, sage and garlic, simmered in broth and soymilk until tender, blended at least 2 minutes and strained, topped with maple-glazed pumpkin seed clusters, pomegranate molasses and orange zest; vegan, 45 minutes, serves 4-6.
glance: 1 1/2-2 pounds butternut, 1/2-inch cubes, lightly browned for flavor
raw green pumpkin seeds toasted with sugar and maple syrup, pomegranate molasses, orange zest
faq: How do I get a velvety smooth soup?

Run the blender for at least 2 minutes, working in batches or with a stick blender, then pass the soup through a very fine sieve or chinois. Add a little more soymilk if needed to reach a nice soup texture.
Should I brown the squash?
For maximum flavor the author browns it; for a brighter color, brown it less and simmer it more.
Can I use the pumpkin seeds elsewhere?
Yes, the glazed seeds are terrific in salads or anywhere you want a little crunch, and the same method works for other nuts, especially walnuts.
How do I make the pumpkin seed clusters?

Toast 1 cup of raw green hulled pumpkin seeds with 1 teaspoon of sugar over medium heat until they start to brown and the sugar melts, add 2 teaspoons maple syrup and a pinch of flaky salt for one more minute, then scrape onto a silicone mat or parchment to cool into clusters.
Is blending hot soup safe?
Be sure you know how to safely puree hot, thick liquids, or allow the soup to cool first.

summary: Brussels sprout gratin with a heretical technique: sprouts par-cooked in the microwave about 5 minutes instead of boiling, combined with a cream reduced on the stovetop with onion, garlic, oregano and nutmeg and a topping of toasted breadcrumbs, baked at 450°F; serves 2 as a side, easily doubled.
glance: 2 as a side dish, easily doubled
1 cup heavy cream reduced until it coats the back of a spoon; no starch added
1 1/2 cups trimmed, microwaved with a few tablespoons of water about 5 minutes until just pierced by a fork
yield: 2 as a side dish, easily doubled
faq: What is a gratin?

Basically anything (usually a vegetable) baked in a shallow dish, often with cream, until the top is crispy: essentially the forerunner of the great American casserole, with fewer ingredients and a little more attention to detail. With Brussels sprouts it brings out their gentle, sweet side.
What is the heresy?

Par-cooking the sprouts in the microwave rather than a big pot of water. The author can almost feel Paul Bocuse staring at him, but the microwave cooks quickly and lightly without sogginess, because heat penetrates to the core of each sprout.
Why cook the components separately?

The downfall of many gratins is timing: the vegetable at perfect tenderness, the sauce thickened and the top crunchy all at once. Cooking all three components separately and combining them just long enough in the oven solves it.
How do I avoid overcooked sprouts?
Microwave about 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until you can just pierce them with a fork; if you smell a cabbagey odor, stop cooking, since overcooked sprouts go into sulfur-smell territory.
Why reduce the cream on the stove?

Rather than counting on the oven to thicken it: cream can be simmered to the desired thickness without scorching or breaking, with no starch added, and reduced heavy cream has a luxurious flavor and mouthfeel.

summary: Spicy tamarind-glazed potatoes, a vegan riff on Thai son-in-law eggs: small potatoes boiled and browned, then glazed with a fiery sauce of dried chiles, garlic, shallot, palm sugar, tamarind concentrate and soy sauce, finished with peanuts, cilantro and green onion; serves 4 in 30 minutes.
glance: 2 pounds very small potatoes, boiled about 10 minutes after the boil, then browned about 8 minutes
10 dried chiles de arbol, garlic, shallot, 1/4 cup palm sugar, 3 tablespoons tamarind concentrate, soy sauce
faq: What are son-in-law eggs?

A famous Thai dish of peeled hard-cooked eggs pan-fried or deep-fried until the outside is wrinkled and brown, then halved and served with a spicy tamarind sauce. This vegan variation uses small potatoes instead of eggs.
How hot is it?
The sauce is quite fiery, but the creamy flesh of the potatoes mitigates the pain. Warn guests not to eat the whole dried chiles, or remove them before serving.
What is tamarind?

The pod of a tropical tree of the same name, with a tart, fruity taste beloved in Southeast Asian, Indian and Mexican cuisines. It's sold as whole pods, semi-dried pulp with seeds, or concentrate; pods and pulp must be soaked, de-skinned and sieved, a messy, tedious job, so the author buys concentrate (often the brand Tamcon) at Asian or Indian groceries.
What do I serve it with?
It's great as a side dish in an Indian meal, or wrapped in a burrito with refried beans and sour cream, which the author and his wife have been known to do.
How do I keep the glaze from burning?
Cook, tossing occasionally, until the sauce is glazing the potatoes, about five more minutes, being careful not to let the sauce burn.

summary: Scallion curd rice: cooked brown rice folded into yogurt tempered with black mustard seeds, ginger and cayenne bloomed in butter, plus six sliced scallions; a way to use leftover rice that serves 4 as a side or light meal.
glance: 4 cups cooked brown rice (about 1 3/4 cups uncooked), room temperature
2 tablespoons black mustard seeds, ginger and cayenne in 3 tablespoons butter, ghee or oil
faq: What is curd rice?

An Indian dish of basmati rice flavored with tangy yogurt, often seasoned with chilis, mustard seeds and curry leaves or cilantro, typically served at the end of multi-course South Indian meals. Here it's a side with dal, curry and Indian pickles, or a light meal on its own.
Why scallions and brown rice?
The author had leftover short-grain brown rice, not basmati, and decided to flavor the curd rice with a whole lot of scallions. He had to arm-wrestle his wife for the last bite.
Which mustard seeds?
Black mustard seeds; don't substitute yellow or brown ones.
Do I need to reheat refrigerated rice?

Yes, even if you want to eat it at room temperature: refrigerated rice starch goes retrograde, becoming crystalline and hard and expelling water, the same process as stale bread. Reheating to around 200 degrees softens the crystals back up.
How do I make it?

Cook the mustard seeds in shimmering butter about 10 seconds, stir in the ginger and cayenne 20 seconds, transfer to a bowl, whisk in the yogurt, salt and pepper, fold in the rice and then the scallions, reserving some for garnish.

summary: Pasta with eggplant and fresh tomatoes, a reinterpreted pasta alla Norma: diced eggplant fried with onion and rosemary, garlic, chili and olives, tossed with a shaped pasta cooked just shy of al dente and finished with raw heirloom tomato, basil, parsley and pecorino; serves 4.
glance: 1 pound strozzapetti or other medium shaped pasta, cooked just shy of al dente; reserve 1 cup pasta water
2 medium, large dice, optionally salted and weighted for an hour first
1 large or 2 medium diced heirloom tomatoes stirred in off the heat, basil, parsley, cheese
Vegetarian; vegan if you omit the cheese; not gluten-free
faq: How is this different from pasta alla Norma?
It's a reinterpretation of the classic Sicilian dish: the author didn't have ricotta salata and wanted to use fresh tomatoes. He says it would also be insanely good with chunks of fresh mozzarella.
What pasta shape should I use?
A medium-sized, shaped pasta (like strozzapetti). With a strand like spaghetti the vegetables won't mix in and it gets irritating to eat.
Do I need to salt the eggplant?

If you have time, toss it with lots of kosher salt in a colander and weight it for an hour to leach out some excess, slightly bitter liquid. If not, it's fine as is: add 2 teaspoons of kosher salt while frying.
How much oil does the eggplant get?
It will absorb all of the 4 tablespoons of canola oil in the pan; don't give it any more. Cook the garlic and chili flakes in the olive oil in a cleared space, then mix in.
When do I add the tomatoes?
Turn off the heat after tossing the pasta with the eggplant mixture and a bit of pasta water, then mix in the diced heirloom tomatoes so they stay fresh.

summary: Goat cheese, asparagus and beet salad with herb flowers: golden beets and asparagus shaved paper-thin, goat cheese balls rolled in toasted sesame and fennel seeds, lemon-balsamic mayonnaise, and chive and rosemary blossoms; serves 4.
glance: 2 medium golden beets boiled, 4 thick asparagus spears blanched 2 minutes, both very thinly sliced
4 ounces chevre rolled in sesame and fennel seeds, at room temperature
8 chive blossoms, 12 rosemary blossoms, minced chive, flaky salt
faq: Why slice the vegetables so thin?

Thin slices create a textural surprise, letting you experience a familiar ingredient in a different way. The author used a Benriner mandoline with a kevlar glove from Microplane for safety; with a sharp knife you won't get such even slices but it would still look and taste delicious.
What are chive and rosemary blossoms?

The chive flowers are purple puffballs with an oniony flavor similar to the herb; rosemary blossoms are much smaller and lighter purple. The author was inspired by another blogger's use of edible flowers.
How do I prepare the beets and asparagus?

Boil the beets in salted water until tender, cool in cold water, peel and slice to the same thickness as the asparagus (optionally cutting 12 uniform circles). Boil the sliced asparagus two minutes and drop in ice water to keep it green.
What is the sauce?

Storebought mayonnaise whisked with lemon juice, very finely cut lemon zest and a pinch of salt, thinned to drizzle, plus a few drops of good balsamic. The author would have preferred a rich lemony hollandaise if time permitted.
How do I plate it?
Place 3 slices of beet and 3 of asparagus on each plate, brush with olive oil, drizzle the lemon sauce, add balsamic drops, a goat cheese ball and the garnishes.

summary: A review of Lauren Chattman's Dessert Express (100 desserts in 30 minutes from desire to first bite) with her chocolate-chili pudding cakes: four ramekins of eggy chocolate batter with cinnamon and cayenne baked about 12 minutes at 375°F until firm at the edges and molten in the center; serves 4.
glance: 375°F for about 12 minutes in 4 six-ounce ramekins; do not overbake
1/2 cup butter, 6 ounces bittersweet chocolate, 3 eggs, 1/3 cup sugar, 1/4 cup flour, cinnamon, cayenne
faq: What is Dessert Express?

A book in which Lauren Chattman gives 100 recipes to get a treat on the table in 30 minutes from desire to first bite. The author says she doesn't shade the truth: no chilling the dough the day before or waiting an extra hour for the oven.
What techniques does she use?

Working in smaller batches, baking in individual servings (mini-muffin tins, ramekins, madeleine pans), pushing temperatures as high as possible, and cooking in nontraditional ways, like pan-frying cookie dough in a waffle iron. The author finds spreading filling on store-bought cookies kind of pointless.
What is a pudding cake?
A cake that is intentionally underbaked a bit so the outside is fairly dry but the inside is still molten chocolate (aka lava cake). You can omit the chili if it doesn't sound good.
How do I make them?

Melt the butter and chocolate in the microwave (30 seconds to 1 minute) and stir smooth; beat the eggs and sugar on high 3 to 5 minutes until pale yellow and thick; stir in the flour, salt, cinnamon and cayenne, then the chocolate; spoon into greased ramekins on a baking sheet.
When are they done?
When the cakes are firm around the edges but still loose in the center, about 12 minutes; let cool 5 minutes on a rack and serve.

summary: Cheddar-battered onion rings: extra-sharp cheddar broiled like a frico, ground to a powder and whisked into a thin tempura-style batter (Morimoto-inspired, with optional xanthan gum), onion rings dredged, dipped and fried at 360°F in small batches; serves 4 in 30 minutes.
glance: 2 cups grated extra-sharp cheddar broiled and ground; 75 g (about 3 ounces) goes in the batter
egg yolk, oil, salt, flour, seltzer; thin like crepe batter
360°F, in small batches, until golden brown
faq: How do you get cheddar flavor into an onion ring?

The author wanted tempura-battered rings that taste like aged cheddar without a melty mess that ruins the crunch, so he broiled the cheese like a frico, then ground it into a powder to add to an otherwise standard tempura batter. The broiling looks like a boiling alien planet as the moisture cooks off and the fat separates.
What is the batter based on?
Chef Morimoto's small-batch tempura, with a pinch of xanthan gum added; the xanthan gum is optional but really helps the batter cling.
How thick should the batter be?
Rather thin, the consistency of crepe batter, not thick pancake batter; add more seltzer as needed.
How do I fry them?

Heat the oil to 360°F. In small batches, dredge each ring in flour (all-purpose or rice), shake off the excess, dip in the batter, drip off the excess and fry until golden brown. Chopsticks make it easiest. Drain on paper towels, pat lightly and season with sea salt.
What do I serve them with?
The author suggests his Stout Chocolate Malt for an Alice in Wonderland spin on traditional diner food.
